answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with earned capacity: each new identity starts as a lone island allowed only tiny transactions, and its limit rises only through a verifiable history of small, honest jobs — like a lagoon that opens to the sea through one narrow channel. A fake identity must therefore do weeks of real work before it can act at scale, and one fraud burns its whole history. Reputation spreads like a zephyr, letting honest agents vouch cheaply, while an attacker pays the full price of genuine work for every fake.
